scope: Q46:B0 only; all four visible texts, every section, full question and supplied theory excerpt reviewed. Java 21 scope. No code/runtime tests.
phase_a: NO_VALID_OPTION confirmed: C's absolute 'только на время CPU-работы' is false/overstated. Java 21 descriptions say VT execute on carriers and may unmount on blocking; they do not state mounted exclusively during CPU work. No alternative fully correct option.

options.label: A
options.wrong_model: Confuses VT with pooled OS threads and ThreadLocal; plausible misconception.
options.facts: Text's claims are wrong, as intended for distractor. Sections correctly state JVM scheduling/carriers but overstate 'no benefit over ExecutorService' and promise 'million vs thousands' as a practical comparison without conditions.

options.label: B
options.wrong_model: Claims VT create CPU parallelism beyond hardware cores; plausible speed/scale confusion.
options.facts: Wrong claim is a valid distractor. Sections overgeneralize 'там работают platform threads' and 'реально хуже для CPU'; API guidance is typically VT for blocking workloads and not long-running CPU-intensive tasks, but does not categorically prohibit VT for CPU work.

options.label: C
options.facts: JVM scheduling/carrier and typical unmount under blocking are broadly right; 'только' falsely limits mounting to CPU time. Sections: scheduler is ForkJoinPool in OpenJDK 21, but blocking/unmount is limited to supported operations; pinning in synchronized/native paths matters. Fixed ~KB/~MB sizes, 100K requests without OOM, 10K+ and Spring Boot auto-use are not guaranteed by Java API; qualify by implementation/resources/configuration. Files/HttpClient blanket claim needs operation-specific qualification.

options.label: D
options.wrong_model: Recasts VT as 1:1 OS threads and denies unmount; plausible platform-thread mental model.
options.facts: False text is suitable as wrong model. Sections accurately describe multiplexing/M:N; 'миллионы' is a scale illustration, not guaranteed for every system.

CONTENT.reason: Each text fully addresses the virtual/platform comparison; however, no valid correct option is established (see phase_a NO_VALID_OPTION). Completeness does not establish factual correctness.

FACTS.reason: No fully correct text: C's 'only CPU work' is too absolute. Multiple sections also overstate scale, executor comparison, CPU thread choice, and no-OOM/performance claims.

LINKAGE.reason: C explanation adds non-guaranteed sizing and unbounded throughput claims; A/B sections draw unsupported categorical conclusions from intended wrong models.

SECTIONS.reason: A if_it_were_true's ExecutorService inference is invalid; A million-vs-thousands lacks constraints. B correction says CPU work 'uses platform' too categorically. C example/when_to_apply make unqualified capacity/framework claims; edge_cases compresses Java 21 pinning details.

SFPL.reason: The prior cue claim is withdrawn: C is 16 words, A 15, B 14, D 18; A also mentions unmount on blocking I/O. Technical accuracy alone is not a formal cue absent subject knowledge. This pass did not establish a structural, punctuation, length, or other objective cue.

ANSC.reason: All four texts state an identifiable, complete misconception/correct model about virtual vs platform threads; none is an omission or fragment.

RU.reason: Understandable, but 'как пул системных потоков', 'монтируются через ThreadLocal между задачами', 'только на время CPU-работы' are awkward/overcompressed; English technical compounds are inconsistently integrated.

findings.label: C
findings.issue: Absolute 'only during CPU work' is not a Java 21 guarantee and rules out other mounted execution.

findings.label: A
findings.issue: ExecutorService comparison does not follow; executors include different implementations and VT per-task executor is itself an ExecutorService.

findings.label: A
findings.issue: 'million VT vs thousands platform' is an unqualified scale promise.

findings.label: B
findings.issue: VT are not categorically excluded from CPU tasks; they are not intended for long-running CPU-intensive work and do not add compute resources.

findings.label: C
findings.issue: Memory sizes, 100K HTTP requests without OOM, 10K+ threshold and framework default are not universal Java 21 guarantees; characterize environmental/configuration limits. Blocking unmount and pinning require supported-operation/JDK-version qualification.

findings.label: D
findings.issue: Scale claim is illustrative only; avoid implying all environments hit an identical OS-thread limit.

sources.verified: Java 21 Thread API: VT are user-mode scheduled by runtime, typically use small carrier set, serve blocked workloads, not intended for long-running CPU-intensive work; daemon threads.
VT are not faster; scale vs latency; blocking I/O can suspend VT and free OS thread; ThreadLocal memory caution; executor creates a VT per task.
Direct open returned HTTP 403; not independently verified in this pass; Oracle Java 21 docs used for claims above.
